title: RW Aurigae

spectrum.method: Forced ePSF photometry on native pixels at the motion-corrected (followed) position in every exposure; wavelength from the spectral WCS at that pixel; inverse-variance means in the 102 SPHEREx/SPIFF bins.

wing_attempt.summary: Experimental wing photometry was attempted on 48 saturated exposures; 48 had enough unflagged pixels to fit, but the release ePSF describes the wings poorly (median reduced chi-square 403), so 2 passed the acceptance cut.

fixed_vs_follow.note: Measured at one fixed sky position, the source keeps 100% of the flux recovered by following its motion (median over 7 bins).

templates.library: SPIFF SPHEREx templates (Gagné et al. 2026; M4–Y0 field, low-gravity and subdwarf grids)

variability.reason: 131 of 142 exposures are saturated or nonlinear at the source. Experimental wing photometry was attempted on 48 saturated exposures; 48 had enough unflagged pixels to fit, but the release ePSF describes the wings poorly (median reduced chi-square 403), so 2 passed the acceptance cut.

halo_variability.method: median surface brightness in an unsaturated ring around the star, compared at matched wavelength

hypotheses.name: Variable astronomical source
evidence: The core is saturated, so brightness was measured from the unsaturated halo (3-5 pixels from the star) at matched wavelength: visit-2 / visit-1 = 0.83 ± 0.05 (3.1 sigma), visit-3 / visit-1 = 0.64 ± 0.04 (6.4 sigma).
Experimental method. On control stars that are not large-amplitude variables the same measurement stays flat (see validation/halo_results.json).

hypotheses.name: Blended or overlapping sources
evidence: RW Aur A and RW Aur B (Gaia DR3 156430822114424576) are 1.4 arcsec apart, far below one SPHEREx pixel: always blended.
1 Gaia DR3 source(s) within 12 arcsec (2 SPHEREx pixels); nearest 1.5 arcsec, G = 12.2.

hypotheses.name: Instrumental or processing artifact
evidence: Detected in too few independent exposures to rule out an artifact.

hypotheses.name: Known solar-system object
evidence: No known asteroid or comet lies within 60 arcsec of the source at any of the 8 observation times checked (IMCCE SkyBoT cone search).

hypotheses.name: Insufficient evidence
evidence: 99 of 142 exposures are saturated at the source core.

verdicts.label: Brightness changed between visits (measured from the unsaturated halo, experimental)

summary.headline: Faded by 36% between visits, measured from its unsaturated halo; its core is saturated.
summary.one_liner: The core saturates the detector, so brightness is measured from the unsaturated ring of light around the star: it faded by 36% between visits (6.4 sigma). An experimental method, checked on stars that do not vary.

limitations: SPHEREx pixels are 6.15 arcsec; sources closer than about 1 pixel are measured as one blend.
Positions are registered to Gaia DR3 field stars with a pure shift per exposure; residual distortion is absorbed into an empirical error floor.
Fluxes use the median pixel solid angle (OMEGA_MEDIAN) and the release ePSF; absolute calibration uncertainties of a few percent are not propagated.
RW Aur B (Gaia DR3 156430822114424576) is about 1.4 arcsec away: always blended in SPHEREx.
follow_up: Use catalogue astrometry (Gaia) or a PSF-wing fit for this bright source; SPHEREx cores are unusable.
Check higher-resolution imaging (e.g. unWISE, 2MASS, Gaia) to separate contributors.

demonstration.title: Comparison star Gaia DR3 156431234433162368 (G = 12.6)
demonstration.why: RW Aurigae saturates SPHEREx, so its own variability cannot be measured here. The same comparison is shown on a real, unsaturated star in the same images: a naive time-ordered light curve mixes wavelengths, while a wavelength-matched comparison isolates genuine change.
